translations.answer: The author replaced the GO1 actuator net with a PD model and retrained it, reporting that the real GO1 no longer kicks legs, shakes, or triggers power protection when velocity commands are zero, and can stand upright when velocity commands are zero. This is an effective workaround in the author's environment; however, since the same thread found inconsistent motor orders and no ablation experiments, the actuator net cannot be considered proven as the sole root cause, and the PD parameters cannot be directly reused as they are not publicly available.
translations.applicability: Only applicable to the author's Orbit/GO1 strategy chain; PD gain, clipping, SDK, and model version are missing, so other robots must retrain and perform low-risk retesting.
translations.credibility.rationale: The environment, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: The maintainer provided code to print joint order and explained the BFS/DFS and height-scan ordering differences.
translations.details.attempts.1: The author replaced the actuator net with a PD model and retrained it.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Print asset.joint_names or asset_cfg.joint_names in the training environment and align it with the real machine SDK, legged-gym, and deployment end observation/action arrays.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: If using height-scan, verify the XY alignment in Isaac Sim/Orbit against the old pipeline's YX order.
translations.details.diagnostics.2: Perform A/B testing of joint order correction and actuator model replacement separately to avoid conflating both changes as a single root cause.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: In the author's specific environment, using a PD model and retraining resulted in the real GO1 no longer kicking legs, shaking, or triggering power protection when velocity commands are zero, and being able to stand upright when velocity commands are zero.
translations.details.environments.0: Orbit/Isaac Lab unitree-go1-flat policy from 2024-04; real Unitree GO1; ONNX Runtime C++; original post did not provide precise submission, SDK, or firmware version.
translations.details.limits.0: Cannot assert all GO1 actuator nets are faulty from this thread.
translations.details.limits.1: No information provided about PD stiffness/damping, action clipping, strategy submission, or real machine SDK version.
translations.details.limits.2: Height-scan is only a maintainer's hint; the original author did not report whether it participated in the strategy.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The real machine symptoms are resolved; however, joint order correction and actuator model replacement were not individually ablated, and the root cause remains unclosed.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: When the Unitree GO1 policy is executed after a strategy upload, it should first verify which interfaces are causing the issue.
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Involves real machine sudden kicking and power protection; re-upload must use a crane or safety rope, low gain, action and torque clipping, emergency stop, and personnel isolation.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The author confirmed that the motor order in legged-gym and Orbit is actually different.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: The author suspects the GO1 actuator net, but the thread does not prove it to be the sole root cause.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Under zero velocity commands, the real GO1 kicks legs, shakes, and triggers power protection.
